chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ashari narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lului, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abu Uthman, from Ali ibn al-Mughira, from Abu Umarah al-Munshid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

He said: He said to me: O Abu Umarah, recite for me about al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both). He said: So I recited and he wept. Then I recited again and he wept. He said: By Allah, I did not cease reciting to him and he continued weeping until I heard the lamentation from the house.

He said: Then he said to me: O Abu Umarah, whoever recites about al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) and makes fifty people weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites poetry about al-Husayn and makes thirty weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and makes twenty weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and makes ten weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and makes even one person weep, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and weeps himself, for him is Paradise. And whoever recites about al-Husayn and feigns crying, for him is Paradise.

key_terms.أنشد: To recite poetry or elegies (inshad), specifically elegiac poetry commemorating the martyrdom of Imam Husayn
key_terms.الجنة: Paradise (Jannah), the ultimate reward promised to those who mourn Husayn
key_terms.بكى: To weep, an act of devotion expressing grief over the tragedy of Karbala
key_terms.تباكى: To feign or endeavor to cry; making an effort to weep even when tears do not come naturally

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting elegies about Imam Husayn and weeping?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) asked Abu Umarah al-Munshid, a renowned poet-reciter, to recite elegies about Imam al-Husayn ibn Ali (AS). As the recitation continued, the Imam wept so profoundly that the weeping spread throughout the household. The Imam then enumerated a descending scale of rewards for those who recite about al-Husayn and move others to tears -- from making fifty people weep down to making even a single person weep, then weeping oneself, and finally even feigning tears -- all meriting Paradise. This hadith, narrated during a gathering on the 8th of Muharram 368 AH, underscores the central importance of mourning for al-Husayn in Shia devotional practice.
